# openlab 0.1.1 Preview

A maintenance preview. The workbench is unchanged; the dependency tree behind it is not.

## Status: early preview

openlab is 0.1.x. We publish it early so the idea improves faster, not because it is finished.

- Expect bugs, and some features that do not work or do not exist yet. The PDF scan engine is
  not bundled.
- Releases can break. Installers are unsigned or signed ad hoc, so macOS asks you to allow the
  first launch and Windows shows SmartScreen.
- Keep your own copy of data, code and results. Until 1.0, treat every workspace as disposable.
- Before 1.0 the version number promises no compatibility: schema, CLI flags and file formats
  may change without a migration path.

If something breaks, open an issue with the version, the platform and the steps.

## What changed

- **The `zip` crate moved from 2.4.2 to 9.7.0.** The old version carried an open advisory
  about archive extraction. openlab only reads an archive's index and never extracts with
  that crate, so nothing was reachable, but the dependency is now clean.
- **The updater plugin moved to 2.14.1**, which drops its own old `zip` and `minisign` copies.
- **libsodium moved to 1.24.6**, the build-time copy that stronghold unpacks.
- No feature changes, no schema changes, no migration.

## Download

| Platform | Build |
| --- | --- |
| macOS (Apple silicon) | `openlab_0.1.1_aarch64.dmg` |
| macOS (Intel) | `openlab_0.1.1_x64.dmg` |
| Windows (x64) | `openlab_0.1.1_x64-setup.exe` |
| Linux (Debian, Ubuntu) | `openlab_0.1.1_amd64.deb` |
| Linux (Fedora, RHEL) | `openlab-0.1.1-1.x86_64.rpm` |
| Linux (portable) | `openlab_0.1.1_amd64.AppImage` |

## macOS: allow the first launch

These preview builds are signed ad hoc, not notarized, so macOS blocks the first launch. This
is expected, and it happens once.

1. Open the DMG and drag **openlab** to **Applications**.
2. Open **System Settings > Privacy & Security** and scroll to **Security**.
3. Next to the message about openlab, click **Open Anyway**.
4. Confirm with **Open**.

Alternatively, right-click **openlab** in Applications and choose **Open**.

A signed and notarized release will open without this step.

## Other platforms

- **Windows:** SmartScreen may warn about the installer. Choose **More info > Run anyway**.
- **Linux:** if the AppImage is not executable, run
  `chmod +x openlab_0.1.1_amd64.AppImage`, then start it as usual.

## About this build

- Free and MIT licensed.
- The optional PDF scan engine (embedding server) is not included in this preview. The rest of
  the workbench works.
- Report issues at https://github.com/sciencedeltacom/openlab/issues.

A signed and notarized 0.1.x release follows once the Apple and Windows signing identities are
configured.
